articles.title: Forget maxxing your life. 2027 must be the year we relax – and start minning | Polly Hudson
articles.summary: Maxxing is selfish, desperately try-hard and often futile. Instead of pushing your endeavours to the limit, minning means doing them less, if at all. Public service announcement: fellow citizens, we have maxxmaxxinged.
body: Maxxing is selfish, desperately try-hard and often futile – surely nobody who ever set out to funmaxx achieved it (see: New Year’s Eve), not even Dua Lipa. Minning is much more noble: it’s about making the world, rather than only yourself, better. Instead of pushing your endeavours to the limit, it means doing them less, if at all.

Back in the days when all of this was fields and we only used one x in “max”, it was clear that max volume is too loud, max capacity too crowded, and max power too draining. Somewhere along the way we lost sight of that. Let’s take a deep breath, and enjoy the relief of leaning into minning. First person to suggest they’re doing maxxminning will be taken to the tower and made an example of.
points: Maxxing is selfish, desperately try-hard and often futile.
Instead of pushing your endeavours to the limit, minning means doing them less, if at all.

articles.title: The kindness of strangers: In 1989 I lost a wallet with $1,000 in it. A couple went to incredible lengths to return it
articles.summary: Cash was king in those days, and that money was enough to last me for a month as I slowly travelled from Australia back to the UK. It was a hot night in 1989 when my wallet – stuffed with $1,000 cash – fell out of my pocket.
body: After university, I left the UK and went travelling in Australia for a year. I saw the delights of the east coast – mostly from various building sites, as I worked my way around doing long hours in the blistering sun. But I loved every minute of it. After 10 months, I had saved enough to make my way slowly back home.
I was enjoying one last night out in Darwin with a gang of traveller friends with whom I was flying to Timor the next day. The intention was to island hop all the way to Singapore.

Cash was king in those days, and the $1,000 I had in my wallet was enough to last me a month on the road. The beers went down easy and I was completely unaware when, at some point in the evening, I lost my wallet. I was still none the wiser when I went to bed to get some sleep before the flight the next morning.
At 1.30am, I awoke to a loud knocking on my door. I stumbled out of bed, bleary-eyed, and opened the door to the hostel manager and an elderly couple – who were holding my wallet.
points: Cash was king in those days, and that money was enough to last me for a month as I slowly travelled from Australia back to the UK.

articles.title: Lymphatic Drainage: 4 Simple Habits to Add to Your Daily Routine
articles.summary: From deep breathing to rebounding, experts explain the small daily habits that can help support healthy lymphatic flow—and why it matters beyond depuffing.
body: Lymphatic drainage has become something of a wellness obsession. From sculpting facial massages to body brushes and compression boots, there are seemingly endless ways to coax away puffiness and encourage a more contoured appearance. But the benefits of a healthy lymphatic system extend well beyond what we can see in the mirror.

The lymphatic system is sometimes described as the “Cinderella of medicine”: “underestimated, yet performing a large part of the essential work,” writes cardiothoracic surgeon Dr. Gerald M. Lemole in his book Lymph & Longevity: The Untapped Secret to Health. While its aesthetic benefits have helped bring lymphatic drainage into the mainstream, this intricate network of vessels, nodes, and fluid is fundamental to everything from immune function to maintaining the body's fluid balance.
And, as it turns out, keeping it functioning properly doesn’t necessarily require a standing appointment with your facialist.

Think of the lymphatic system as the body’s behind-the-scenes maintenance crew. Working alongside the circulatory and immune systems, it helps collect excess fluid from tissues, transports immune cells, and carries certain waste products away from cells.

articles.title: 13 Books That Changed Comedian, Author, and Drag King Murray Hill’s Life
articles.summary: Hill’s new memoir, “Showbiz!: My Life as a Middle-Aged Man,” is out now from Gallery Books.
body: Hollywood is a strange and mysterious place, even for those who have operated within its orbit for decades. But author, comedian, and drag king Murray Hill’s new memoir, Showbiz!: My Life as a Middle-Aged Man (Gallery Books), sheds an alternately moving and hilarious light on “the industry,” charting Hill’s rise from a fraught New England childhood to a career starring in New York and Boston cabaret shows and appearing on television series including Somebody, Somewhere, Life & Beth, and Elsbeth.
In the latest edition of Vogue ’s Required Reading series, Hill shares a selection of books that have inspired his own memoir and seen him through the ups and downs of Hollywood life.

Kathleen Hanna is a punk-rock icon, feminist trailblazer, and one of my dearest friends. She’s spent her life making noise, breaking rules, and telling the establishment to beat it. What I love about this book is how she writes about the messy, painful, and hilarious realities behind being a revolutionary. She built her own stage, grabbed the microphone, and started a movement. She is my forever inspiration.

articles.title: Ahead of Season 4, The Gilded Age Cast Celebrated in New York and L.A.
articles.summary: Ahead of The Gilded Age’s return to screens on November 1, dual celebrations on each coast saw the cast reunite for a red carpet outing at The Plaza and an elegant bash at Greystone Mansion in Beverly Hills.
body: At this week’s lavish season 4 premiere party at The Plaza, Carrie Coon, Cynthia Nixon, Audra McDonald, and their fellow stars left their bustles behind. After three seasons of elaborate period costumes, you’d think slipping into a corset every day would make dressing up for a night out a breeze. Alas, think again.

“It’s so much harder to get ready for a red carpet than it is for work,” Coon, clad in an Acne Studios gown, told Vogue. “My dresser, Amber, helps me get into my costumes and cinch my waist from a 28 to a 24. It takes about six minutes and 30 seconds to take off my costumes and wigs. Red carpets are way more stressful, and sometimes the clothes are just as challenging. For me, it’s the shoes. When you get to 16 hours in three-inch heels, you start to lose your mind!”

articles.title: At This Manhattan Halloween Party, 250 People Came Dressed as Dolly Parton
articles.summary: The Frankie Shop and Unemployed paid homage to the late Dolly Parton with their raucous Halloween party at Ella Funt in Manhattan.
body: On Friday evening, swarms of Dolly Parton lookalikes took over the East Village for The Frankie Shop and Unemployed’s fourth annual Halloween bash. This year, the festivities tipped a rhinestone-covered cowboy hat to the late, great country music icon, with platinum-blonde bouffants, exaggerated bust lines, and plenty of pink as far as the eye could see.

By 10:30 p.m., guests sauntered downstairs to the basement club beneath Ella Funt, the East Village bistro turned late-night hotspot. The subterranean space was as ample as Dolly’s most famous asset—a surprising rarity in downtown Manhattan. Given the theme, it felt like a cross between a Brooklyn warehouse and a Dollywood fever dream, with the wood paneling and hot-pink walls illuminated by a soft rosy glow. At the center of it all was a sunken black-and-white checkered dance floor, though you could barely make out the floor underneath all the dancing Dollys.
points: The Frankie Shop and Unemployed paid homage to the late Dolly Parton with their raucous Halloween party at Ella Funt in Manhattan.

articles.title: Salted Coffee Custard Pie
articles.summary: Like a fine cappuccino, but make it pie. The big bonus here is the buttery oatmeal cookie crust—which requires zero pie weights during prebake.
body: If you can’t be fussed with making coffee and dessert after a big holiday dinner, consider this twofer instead. The silky, sliceable, cool custard is rich and intense with two kinds of coffee, while the oatmeal crust is a tweedy-textured study in contrast. It’s prebaked to mitigate sogginess but doesn’t require pie weights. Mascarpone keeps the whipped cream firm and fluffy for a full 24 hours.

Don’t be tempted to skip the cold-brew concentrate. You don’t want regular cold brew, and definitely not brewed and cooled coffee from your coffee machine at home, no matter how fancy. The concentrate (highly recommend Grady’s Cold Brew Coffee Concentrate) is consistent every single time with exactly the right strength to stand up to the dairy and eggs in the filling.
